audit_findings.title: Parent-common numerator is mixed with consolidated cash-flow add-backs and cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed NCI equity was $129 million at June 30, 2026 and FY2025 NCI income was $45 million, equal to 13.1% of the $344.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A and cash enter OE and the bridge, while attributable net income and parent shares exclude minority claims; consolidated capital expenditures may also contain minority-funded spending.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Cabot and its wholly-owned subsidiaries and majority-owned and controlled subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, although its net dollar effect is not. The filed NCI earnings are large relative to the anchor, so assigning any material minority share of add-backs or cash to parent holders could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every historical and current OE component on a Cabot-attributable basis and identify the parent-owned portion of the $250 million cash balance, including subsidiary-level D&A, capital expenditures, cash and ownership percentages; rerun all scenarios and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The operating anchor may be stale for a known down year
audit_findings.magnitude: Nine-month FY2026 Segment EBIT fell $74 million, including a $97 million Reinforcement Materials decline; attributable net income fell $141 million versus the prior-year period
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation begins projected OE from the $344.3 million FY2025-based anchor without incorporating the FY2026 operating step-down.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect EBIT in our Reinforcement Materials segment to decline driven by our expectation for the outcomes of our annual tire customer agreements to be lower in calendar 2026 as compared to calendar 2025 given the impact of tire trade flows on the regional demand for our product and a challenging macroeconomic backdrop.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated stale-anchor problem, not merely a forecast risk. FY2026 filings confirm substantially weaker Reinforcement Materials profitability, while the valuation updated only the balance-sheet bridge. Because bear value of $80.88 is already $0.60 below the $81.48 market price, a lower current OE run rate can plainly affect the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate attributable OE for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, remove only documented nonrecurring items, estimate the fourth quarter from filed guidance, reset the starting OE before applying scenario growth and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory environmental spending may have been treated as removable growth capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $74 million of FY2025 environmental capital expenditures and approximately $60 million anticipated for FY2026, equal to 21.5% and 17.4% of the $344.3 million anchor respectively; any omitted portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Understating enduring maintenance and compliance capital expenditure directly overstates recurring OE; additional emissions-credit and control-equipment operating costs would also reduce OE or growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Increasing regulatory programs associated with emissions and concerns regarding climate change are expected to increase our capital and operational costs in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: An omission is not demonstrated because the supplied OE reconciliation does not show what maintenance capex already includes. However, the filed compliance-spending scale is large enough to change value materially if excluded, and future Sarnia and EU requirements indicate that the burden does not end with the completed U.S. controls.
audit_findings.action: Map each FY2025 and FY2026 environmental project to the maintenance-capex deduction, separate genuinely one-time installation work from recurring replacement and compliance needs, quantify ongoing operating and emissions-credit costs, then rerun OE using the sustainable annual burden without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Legacy respirator liabilities are an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $32 million reserve at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.60 per valuation share and 0.6% of the $5.087 billion base equity value; possible adverse development is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement of previously accrued claims may not reduce future net income, so omitting the reserve from both forecast OE and the equity bridge overstates common equity; reserve increases would enlarge the effect.
audit_findings.evidence: Because reserves are limited to amounts that are probable and estimable as of a relevant measurement date, and there is inherent difficulty in projecting the impact of potential developments on Cabot’s share of liability for these existing and future claims, it is reasonably possible that the liabilities for existing and future claims could change in the near term and that change could be material.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing reserve is a demonstrated unbridged claim but is small relative to base equity value and by itself would not overturn the base conclusion. The filing nevertheless states that near-term reserve changes could be material, and that unquantified tail prevents a NOT_MATERIAL determination for the finding as a whole.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether forecast OE includes the reserve's expected cash unwind; if not, deduct the $32 million once in the bridge. Obtain the claim-rollforward assumptions and sensitivity range used for the audited reserve and rerun the bridge for supported adverse-development cases.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter may omit the Mexico acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $68 million purchase price, equal to 1.3% of base equity value or $1.27 per valuation share; $66 million net cash paid and $26 million post-close revenue, the latter equal to 0.7% of FY2025 sales
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted acquired earnings understate OE, while omitted incremental interest or assumed obligations overstate OE; the June 2026 cash balance already reflects the acquisition payment.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 4, 2025, Cabot entered into an agreement with Bridgestone Corporation to purchase its carbon black manufacturing facility, Mexico Carbon Manufacturing, S.A. de C.V., in Tamaulipas, Mexico for approximately $ 70 million, which will be subject to customary closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition omission is demonstrated: it closed January 31, 2026 and entered Reinforcement Materials results. Its disclosed scale is small relative to the $5.087 billion base equity value and consolidated revenue, while the $250 million bridge cash is already post-acquisition. The available numbers therefore do not indicate capacity to change the overall conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Add post-close MXCB EBIT, attributable D&A, maintenance capex, working-capital needs, integration costs and incremental financing expense to the perimeter reconciliation; verify that the $66 million net payment is not deducted again, and confirm the conclusion with a perimeter-consistent rerun.

audit_findings.title: A non-cash tax valuation-allowance adjustment may remain in normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $31 million FY2025 non-cash tax expense, equal to 8.9% of FY2025 OE and 9.0% of the $344.3 million anchor; resulting trend and valuation effects are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If left in attributable net income without normalization, the non-cash valuation-allowance expense depresses FY2025 OE and may lower the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on updated forecasts of future taxable income and changes in tax laws, the Company determined that it is more likely than not that a portion of its tax credit carryforwards would not be realizable and increased the valuation allowance recorded against its U.S. Deferred tax assets by $ 31 million for fiscal 2025, compared to a non-cash income tax benefit of $ 24 million recorded in fiscal 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $31 million non-cash charge is demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE reconciliation already removed it. Even if unadjusted, the anchor uses a multi-year trend rather than FY2025 OE directly, so the supplied information cannot establish the resulting anchor or valuation change.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation for the valuation-allowance adjustment, remove it only if still embedded, preserve a sustainable cash-tax charge, recompute the full log trend and rerun all scenarios.
